title: Making a triglyceride
caption: Each of glycerol's three –OH groups condenses with the –COOH of a fatty acid, forming an ester bond and releasing a molecule of water: three ester bonds, three waters. Lipase reverses it. The chains are drawn short (8 carbons) to fit; in fats they are typically 14–22.
alt: Glycerol and three molecules of octanoic acid react to give the triglyceride tricaprylin and three molecules of water.
description: Three fatty acids (here octanoic acid, C₈H₁₆O₂, a short one for clarity), each with a –COOH group.
Three condensation reactions form three ester bonds, giving tricaprylin, C₂₇H₅₀O₆.
Three molecules of water are released: C₃H₈O₃ + 3 C₈H₁₆O₂ = C₂₇H₅₀O₆ + 3 H₂O.
